passage: Read the following passage carefully and answer the questions given below it. In an era characterized by relentless comparison, the pursuit of personal excellence is frequently overshadowed by the compulsion to outperform others. This externalization of ambition subtly distorts the purpose of effort, transforming growth into a competitive spectacle rather than an inward journey. Individuals, consequently, begin to calibrate their worth against fluctuating benchmarks, mistaking visibility for value. Such dependence on external validation not only destabilizes self-perception but also fosters a fragile sense of achievement that is contingent upon constant reinforcement. Paradoxically, genuine progress often necessitates a withdrawal from this comparative paradigm. When individuals reorient their focus toward intrinsic standards, they cultivate a more resilient and autonomous sense of purpose. However, this shift demands a deliberate disengagement from societal metrics that equate success with recognition. Those who undertake this transition may initially encounter dissonance, as their efforts lack immediate affirmation. Yet, over time, this internal anchoring engenders a deeper, more sustainable form of fulfillment. Thus, authentic excellence is less a function of surpassing others and more an outcome of sustained alignment between one’s aspirations and actions.
